plan.planning_summary: Refining route_01 based on iteration_15 success (best_target_score: 0.9094) and feedback directives. Three complementary routes explore: (1) 24-layer stack with ±20% perturbation and simulated annealing to escape local minima, (2) 28-layer stack with same optimization strategy to test layer count scaling, (3) 20-layer stack with different quarter-wave reference wavelength (650 nm vs 550 nm) to probe stopband centering effects. All routes maintain HfO2/SiO2 alternating topology on fused silica substrate with air incidence, normal unpolarized illumination, and coherent TMM treatment across 400-1565 nm spectrum.

routes.title: 24-Layer Dual-Band Filter with Simulated Annealing and ±20% Perturbation
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 20 to 24 while applying simulated annealing with ±20% thickness perturbation around quarter-wave initialization will enable the optimizer to escape local minima observed in iteration_15 and achieve higher dual-band spectral separation scores through broader search space exploration.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave Bragg stack principle with stopband centered near 550 nm for visible rejection, optimized thickness distribution to maintain telecom band transmission while maximizing visible reflectance. Simulated annealing allows temporary acceptance of worse solutions to cross energy barriers between thickness basins.

routes.execution_request_english: Design and optimize a 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2 (24 finite layers total). Initialize thicknesses at quarter-wave optical thickness for 550 nm reference wavelength (HfO2: ~68.75 nm, SiO2: ~94.83 nm assuming n_HfO2≈2.0, n_SiO2≈1.46). Apply ±20% perturbation bounds around initialization values. Use simulated annealing optimizer with temperature schedule over first 50 iterations to enable cross-basin exploration. Optimize for mean transmittance maximization in 1530-1565 nm band and mean reflectance maximization in 400-700 nm band at normal unpolarized incidence. Treat all layers as coherent. Compute spectrum from 400-1565 nm with sufficient resolution to capture both bands. Include relative uniform thickness tolerance analysis for robustness scoring. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
routes.revision_reason: Responds to feedback directive to increase thickness initialization perturbation to ±20% and apply simulated annealing temperature schedule during first 50 iterations. Increases layer count from 20 to 24 to test scaling while staying within 30-layer manufacturing constraint.

routes.title: 20-Layer Dual-Band Filter with 650 nm Quarter-Wave Reference and Simulated Annealing

routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave Bragg stack with stopband centered at 650 nm instead of 550 nm, positioning the high-reflectance region closer to the red edge of visible spectrum while maintaining sufficient bandwidth to cover 400-700 nm. Tests whether stopband centering affects dual-band performance balance.

research_influence: Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:92993850:s2chunk:92993850:1765:3736:69b2ad685bc8c493 confirms telecom C-band (1550 nm) importance for satellite quantum communication, motivating the 1530-1565 nm transmission objective but does not provide specific thin-film design methods.

No literature evidence was found for optimal thickness distribution, material choice constraints, objective formulation, or optimization strategy - all routes rely on theory-based thin-film interference principles and transfer matrix method.

Prior iteration_15 success (best_target_score: 0.9094) establishes 20-layer 550 nm quarter-wave baseline; refinement routes test whether layer count scaling or stopband recentering can improve performance.
unresolved_decisions: Optimal layer count between 20-30 layers remains unknown - routes test 20, 24, and 28 to identify performance saturation point.
Optimal quarter-wave reference wavelength (550 nm vs 650 nm vs other values) for maximizing 400-700 nm reflectance while maintaining 1530-1565 nm transmission.
Whether simulated annealing provides meaningful improvement over gradient-based optimization for this specific thickness landscape.
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
